simple.meaning: שְׂלָו (sᵉlâv) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “the quail collectively (as slow in flight from its weight).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 4 times across Exodus, Numbers, Psalms, beginning at Exodus 16:13. Its meaning is built by comparing the passages where Scripture uses it.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שְׂלָו (H7958).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: שְׂלָו (sᵉlâv) / H7958 is traced through Exodus 16:13, Numbers 11:31, Numbers 11:32, Psalms 105:40 as a generated source-based concept entry.

firstOccurrence.englishText: In the evening, quail came up and covered the camp; and in the morning the dew lay around the camp.

majorEvents.label: Movement or place
majorEvents.evidenceText: A wind from Yahweh went out and brought quails from the sea, and let them fall by the camp, about a day’s journey on this side, and a day’s journey on the other side, around the camp, and about two cubits‡ A cubit is the length from the tip of the middle finger to the elbow on a man’s arm, or about 18 inches or 46 centimeters. above the surface of the earth.

timeline.evidenceText: In the evening, quail came up and covered the camp; and in the morning the dew lay around the camp.

A wind from Yahweh went out and brought quails from the sea, and let them fall by the camp, about a day’s journey on this side, and a day’s journey on the other side, around the camp, and about two cubits‡ A cubit is the length from the tip of the middle finger to the elbow on a man’s arm, or about 18 inches or 46 centimeters. above the surface of the earth.

The people rose up all that day, and all of that night, and all the next day, and gathered the quails. He who gathered least gathered ten homers; § 1 homer is about 220 liters or 6 bushels and they spread them all out for themselves around the camp.
They asked, and he brought quails,

definitions.short: the quail collectively (as slow in flight from its weight)
definitions.full: H7958. selav שְׂלָו noun feminine Exod 16:13 quail (probably foreign word; Arabic , Syriac , Samaritan ); — quail, coturnix communis or vulguris (Tristr NHB 229 ff. FFP 124 Post Hast. DB. QUAIL , Di 16:13 ): — absolute collective Num 11:32 (J), Exod 16:13 (P), Psa 105:40 (in all Qr שְׂלָיו ); plural שַׂלְוִים Num 11:31 (J; as if from singular שַׂלְוֶה ). שַׂלְמָא , I. שַׂלְמָה see שַׂלְמוֺן . below II. שַׂלְמָה = שִׂמְלָה see below שׂמל .
definitions.rootNote: or שְׂלָיו ; by orthographical variation from 7951 through the idea of sluggishness ;
